candidates.title: Secondary adrenal insufficiency prevalence in patients with euvolaemic hyponatraemia - analysis of a randomized controlled, parallel-group trial (standard care versus guideline based).
candidates.abstract: In patients with euvolaemic hyponatraemia, secondary adrenal insufficiency (SAI) is a rare but important differential diagnosis of the syndrome of inappropriate antidiuresis (SIAD). This study aimed to characterise the clinical presentation and management of SAI. Secondary analysis of a randomized, controlled, multicentre hyponatraemia trial (plasma sodium <130 mmol/L). Patients were randomised either to a guideline-based targeted plasma sodium correction arm (intervention) managed by the study team, or a standard-of-care arm (control) where diagnosis, including cortisol measurements, and treatment were up to the treating physician. Patients diagnosed with euvolaemic hyponatraemia due to SAI or SIAD were included. Among 1074 euvolaemic patients, SIAD was present in 79.8% (n= 859) and SAI in 2.9% (n= 31), including 19 newly diagnosed and 12 pre-existing cases. Other common causes were primary polydipsia (14.5%, n= 156), thiazide-induced euvolaemic hyponatraemia (0.5%, n= 5) and hypothyroidism (0.3%, n= 3). SAI patients had significantly lower plasma sodium levels (121 vs. 127 mmol/L) and lower systolic blood pressure (118 vs. 130 mmHg) than SIAD patients. Hypopituitarism was the leading cause of SAI (38.7%), followed by exogenous glucocorticoid use (19.4%) and immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy (16.1%). In the standard-of-care arm, cortisol was measured in only 28.9% of patients with suspected SIAD. In newly diagnosed SAI patients, time to diagnosis and treatment was one day. In the entire SAI group, hydrocortisone increased plasma sodium from 121 to 136 mmol/L and normalised hyponatraemia in 71% after 2.5 days of admission. In SIAD, plasma sodium increased from 127 to 134 mmol/L and normalised in 45% after 4 days. SAI is a rare but clinically relevant cause of euvolaemic hyponatraemia, yet diagnostic evaluation is often insufficient. Lower plasma sodium and blood pressure should prompt consideration of SAI. When identified, treatment was rapid and associated with more frequent plasma sodium normalisation than in SIAD.

candidates.title: Acute diencephalic syndrome after transventricular resection of giant pituitary adenomas with third ventricular extension: clinical course and association with extent of resection.
candidates.abstract: To describe acute diencephalic syndrome (ADS) after superior transventricular surgery for giant pituitary adenomas with true third-ventricular extension, and to explore the association of ADS with extent of resection in a selected cohort. We retrospectively analyzed 40 adults operated on in 2015-2025 (23 total, 17 subtotal resections; 22 anterior transcallosal and 18 transcortical transventricular approaches). Postoperative AVP-D was distinguished from multidomain ADS, graded retrospectively according to the previously published four-stage framework. Final-stage agreement was reassessed independently in all 40 patients. Postoperative AVP-D occurred in all 40 patients; four had isolated AVP-D without ADS. ADS occurred in 36/40 (90.0%): 23/23 after total and 13/17 after subtotal resection (risk difference 23.5 percentage points; 95% Newcombe CI 3.5-47.3; two-sided Fisher exact p = 0.026). Stage III-IV ADS occurred in 9/23 versus 3/17 (p = 0.179). Independent final-stage agreement was 36/40 (90.0%; linear-weighted κ = 0.926). Five patients required mechanical ventilation, and two died. ADS was frequent in this anatomically selected transventricular cohort, but the operational definition is not specific for hypothalamic injury and the observational comparison is vulnerable to confounding by indication. The observed lower ADS frequency after subtotal resection is hypothesis-generating. Prospective multicenter validation is necessary.

candidates.title: Adrenal vein thrombosis during pregnancy or the postpartum period: a systematic review.
candidates.abstract: Adrenal vein thrombosis (AVT) is a rare but potentially life-threatening condition that may present as nonspecific abdominal or lower back pain during pregnancy and may be overlooked because of overlapping obstetric or gastrointestinal symptoms. AVT remains poorly characterized epidemiologically, and its management is not supported by robust evidence or consensus-based recommendations. To improve diagnosis and management, we searched the MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, ScienceDirect and Cochrane Library databases up until October 2025 for publications on AVT in pregnancy and postpartum. Thirty-eight articles reporting 73 AVT episodes in 71 patients (three retrospective studies, five case series and thirty case reports) were reviewed. Presentation was consistent but nonspecific: mainly acute abdominal (74.4%) or lower back pain (49.3%), often associated with nausea (23.3%) and vomiting (31.5%). Events occurred predominantly in the third trimester (79.6%), at a mean ± standard deviation gestational age of 31±5.7 weeks. Most cases were unilateral (63/72, 87.5%) and right-sided (48/72, 66.7%). Diagnosis relied mainly on contrast-enhanced abdominal computed tomography (56/73, 76.7%). Imaging evidenced adrenal necrosis and hemorrhage in 88.9% and 8.3% of cases, respectively. Adrenal insufficiency requiring hydrocortisone occurred in 17.1% of cases and was mainly associated with bilateral AVT. Low-molecular-weight heparin was the preferred anticoagulant during the acute phase (81.8%), followed by a switch to an oral anticoagulant postpartum (25.7%). The median treatment duration was of 24 weeks. Opioids analgesics were required in 54.8% of cases. This review summarizes the clinical presentation, diagnostic findings, management, and outcomes of AVT during pregnancy and postpartum.
candidates.journal: Journal of thrombosis and haemostasis : JTH

candidates.title: Pituicytoma Presenting With Hypogonadotropic Hypogonadism in a Highly Vascular Sellar and Suprasellar Mass: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Pituicytoma is a rare low-grade tumor arising from the pituicyte lineage of the posterior pituitary and infundibular region. Because its clinical and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) features overlap with those of more common sellar tumors and because it is often highly vascular, preoperative diagnosis and surgical management can be challenging. We presented a 45-year-old man who presented with four years of fatigue, reduced libido, erectile dysfunction, and intermittent frontal headache. Early-morning biochemical testing showed low total testosterone (8.9 nmol/L), with inappropriately normal luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), consistent with secondary hypogonadism. Pituitary magnetic resonance imaging showed a 25 × 28 × 27 mm sellar and suprasellar mass with cavernous sinus extension and superior displacement of the optic chiasm; radiologically, the lesion was initially interpreted as a pituitary macroadenoma. Because of concern regarding vascularity, computed tomography (CT) cerebral angiography was performed and demonstrated a hypertrophied right meningo-hypophyseal trunk supplying the tumor. Due to the anticipated risk of major intraoperative hemorrhage, partial surgical debulking was performed. Histopathology and immunohistochemistry supported the diagnosis of pituicytoma. Testosterone replacement increased serum testosterone. Six weeks after surgery, the patient developed secondary adrenal insufficiency and was commenced on hydrocortisone replacement. Radiotherapy was planned for the substantial residual tumor. This case highlights the importance of considering pituicytoma in the differential diagnosis of an enhancing sellar or suprasellar mass with pituitary dysfunction, particularly when marked vascularity is suspected. Preoperative vascular assessment and multidisciplinary management are important when complete resection may carry substantial hemorrhagic risk.

candidates.title: Identification and monitoring of immune-related adverse reactions of PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors based on symptom network analysis.
candidates.abstract: PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors have become first-line cancer therapies by disrupting immune checkpoint downregulation, thereby potentiating antitumor immunity. However, this enhanced immune activation may also target normal tissues, triggering multisystemic immune-related adverse events (irAE) that complicate clinical management. Conventional pharmacovigilance analyses typically assess individual adverse events in isolation, limiting the ability to capture inter-symptom relationships. Symptom network analysis, an emerging computational approach, constructs co-occurrence networks to identify core symptoms, key associations, and bridge nodes across organ systems, thus enabling a systematic understanding of complex suspected irAE profiles. Adverse event records for six PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors were extracted from two spontaneous reporting databases: FAERS (Q1 2005-Q3 2024) and JADER (Q1 2004-Q1 2025). Potential signals were screened using reporting odds ratio(ROR), proportional reporting ratio(PRR), and multivariate gamma-Poisson shrinkage (MGPS) methods. Symptom co-occurrence networks were subsequently constructed using EBIC-GLASSO based on Tetrachoric correlation matrices, which are specifically designed for binary adverse event data and correct for attenuation due to dichotomization. Four centrality metrics-Strength, Closeness, Betweenness, and Expected Influence-were calculated via the qgraph package. The bootnet package performed 1,000 bootstrap iterations to evaluate 95% confidence intervals for edge weights and centrality stability coefficients. In FAERS, nivolumab (48,330) and pembrolizumab (37,224) generated the highest report volumes. PD-1 inhibitor networks consistently centered on a systemic-gastrointestinal symptom cluster comprising decreased appetite, fatigue, diarrhea, and nausea, whereas PD-L1 inhibitor networks additionally featured prominent hematologic abnormalities. In JADER, interstitial lung disease and adrenal insufficiency emerged as central nodes, reflecting cross-database differences in reporting patterns and physician-initiated reporting practices. Strength and Expected Influence centrality metrics showed good to excellent stability (CS ≥ 0.672 in most networks), supporting the robustness of the core symptom clusters. Symptom network analysis effectively delineates core suspected irAE symptoms and inter-system associations for PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors. FAERS-derived networks emphasize systemic-gastrointestinal syndromes, while JADER reveals pulmonary-endocrine predominance in Japanese populations. These findings demonstrate the utility of symptom network analysis as a complementary approach to traditional pharmacovigilance for characterizing complex suspected irAE patterns across different data sources and populations.

candidates.title: Long-term metabolic and biochemical outcomes of pasireotide LAR in resistant acromegaly.
candidates.abstract: Pasireotide long‑acting release (PAS‑LAR) is a second‑generation somatostatin receptor ligand approved for patients with acromegaly resistant/intolerant to first‑generation analogues or combination medical therapy. Real‑world evidence on its metabolic impact and tumour response remains limited. To evaluate the long‑term efficacy, metabolic safety, and tumour effects of PAS‑LAR in a real‑life cohort of acromegalic patients. This was a single-centre, retrospective observational study conducted at a tertiary endocrine centre in Romania. Thirty acromegalic patients previously treated with first-generation somatostatin receptor ligands (fg-SRLs) ± pegvisomant ± cabergoline were switched to PAS-LAR ± cabergoline. Data were collected at baseline, after 3- and 6-months of PAS-LAR treatment, and at the last available visit (median 36.5 months). Thirty patients (66.7% female; mean age 44.4 ± 12.0 years) were treated with PAS-LAR for a mean duration of 44.4 ± 31.2 months. IGF-1 xULN decreased from 1.64 ± 0.79 at baseline to 0.99 ± 0.44 at the last visit (p < 0.0001), with strict disease control (IGF-1 xULN ≤ 1.0) achieved in 60.0% of patients. Acceptable biochemical control (IGF-1 < 1.3 xULN) increased from 26.7% to 76.7% (p < 0.001). Random GH decreased from 4.26 ± 5.38 to 1.58 ± 1.43 ng/mL (p < 0.001). Median HbA1c increased from 5.65% (IQR 5.50-5.90) to 6.20% (IQR 6.03-6.88; p < 0.001). New-onset diabetes occurred in 9/24 (37.5%) patients without diabetes at baseline. At the last evaluation, HbA1c was ≥ 7.0% in 6 patients (20.0%). In exploratory analyses, higher diagnostic IGF-1 xULN correlated with greater increases in FPG (rho = 0.562, p = 0.001) and HbA1c (rho = 0.555, p = 0.001). Exploratory analyses suggested that higher IGF-1 levels at diagnosis may be associated with greater glycemic deterioration during follow-up. This potential association requires confirmation in larger cohorts. Hyperglycemic events are frequent but largely manageable with standard antidiabetic therapy. Lipid parameters remain stable or improve slightly. Early glucose monitoring should be standard during PAS‑LAR therapy.

candidates.title: Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumors in the Pediatric Population.
candidates.abstract: Pediatric pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PPitNETs) are rare but present significant clinical challenges in children. Their diverse presentations necessitate comprehensive endocrinologic and radiographic evaluation. They are most commonly prolactin-secreting or adrenocorticotropic hormone-secreting. A genetic mutation can be present, particularly in young patients with aggressive disease. Management is multidisciplinary. Medical therapy is first-line treatment of prolactinomas, and surgery is first-line treatment of most other PPitNETs, with reasonable remission rates when performed in experienced centers. Long-term outcomes are favorable, although hypopituitarism and lifelong hormone replacement remain important concerns. Ongoing surveillance is essential to ensure detect recurrence, and monitor treatment-related complications.

candidates.title: 2026 consensus on the management of Cushing's disease: a collaborative statement from the Korean Endocrine Society and Japan Endocrine Society.
candidates.abstract: The primary treatment goal of Cushing's disease (CD) is sustained normalization of hypercortisolism as well as relief of tumor mass effects, to reduce morbidity and mortality and improve long-term quality of life. Korea and Japan share broadly similar therapeutic principles for CD; however, real-world management differs because of country-specific healthcare systems, regulatory environments, and medication availability. Building on the previously published Korean Endocrine Society (KES)-Japan Endocrine Society (JES) diagnostic consensus, a joint multidisciplinary working group developed an expert consensus focused on the treatment and management of CD. Surgical intervention for pituitary tumors, primarily via a transsphenoidal approach, remains the first-line treatment when feasible. Subsequent treatment should be individualized according to disease and tumor characteristics, severity of hypercortisolism, associated comorbidities, and regional availability of therapeutic options. Medical treatment is recommended for patients with persistent or recurrent disease after surgery, for those who are not candidates for surgery or who decline surgical intervention, and as bridging therapy in severe cases requiring urgent control of hypercortisolemia or when definitive treatment is delayed. Pituitary tumor-directed agents and adrenal steroidogenesis inhibitors constitute key pharmacologic options, but the available agents and reimbursement status differ between Korea and Japan. Radiation therapy is considered when surgery is not feasible or when control is not achieved with surgery and/or medical therapy, and bilateral adrenalectomy may be reserved for highly selected refractory cases. This consensus statement provides harmonized, practice-oriented recommendations while acknowledging current evidence gaps and the need for further collaborative research to inform CD management in East Asian populations.

candidates.title: Multidisciplinary Approach to Functioning Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumors.
candidates.abstract: Functioning pituitary neuroendocrine tumors require individualized multidisciplinary management because of both tumor mass effects and hormone hypersecretion. Evaluation includes biochemical assessment of hormone excess, pituitary imaging, visual and cranial nerve examination, and assessment of comorbidities. Surgical resection, most commonly via an endoscopic endonasal transsphenoidal approach, is the primary treatment for most functioning tumors. However, prolactinomas are generally treated with dopamine agonists, whereas surgery is typically first-line for growth hormone-, adrenocorticotropic hormone-, and thyroid-stimulating hormone-secreting tumors. Persistent or recurrent disease may require repeat surgery, medical therapy, or radiation.

candidates.title: Oropouche fever in a changing tropical world: emergence, diagnostics and surveillance preparedness for India.
candidates.abstract: Oropouche virus (OROV) is an emerging arthropod-borne virus causing Oropouche fever. OROV is transmitted predominantly by the biting midge Culicoides paraensis. Although historically confined to South America, imported cases have been reported, highlighting its expanding geographic range and global public health relevance. Currently, there are no commercially available diagnostic assays for laboratory confirmation of OROV infection. In addition, no specific antiviral therapy or licensed vaccine is available. The recent emergence of cases outside traditional endemic areas further emphasizes the urgent need to address critical knowledge gaps. This review critically synthesizes current evidence on OROV virology, transmission dynamics, clinical spectrum and diagnostic challenges. We further contextualize OROV within the Indian setting, where competent Culicoides vectors are present, and discuss the importance of incorporating OROV into targeted surveillance and travel-related screening frameworks to facilitate early detection, reduce diagnostic misclassification and strengthen one-health preparedness in regions currently considered non-endemic.

candidates.title: Subarachnoid Pneumocephalus Following Endoscopic Transsphenoidal Surgery.
candidates.abstract: A 26-year-old man with past medical history of prolactinoma presented two weeks status post endoscopic transsphenoid prolactinoma excision with a positional headache and cerebrospinal fluid rhinorrhea; he was found to have diffuse subarachnoid air. There are few reports of subarachnoid pneumocephalus in the emergency medicine literature. Pneumocephalus, particularly tension pneumocephalus, typically occurs in the setting of traumatic skull fractures. However, emergency physicians should be aware of subarachnoid pneumocephalus in the setting of endoscopic skull base surgeries.
candidates.journal: Clinical practice and cases in emergency medicine

candidates.title: Deep learning MGMT promoter methylation status prediction in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma using multiparametric MRI: Benchmark vs. real‑world performance.
candidates.abstract: Preoperative determination of O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase (MGMT) promoter methylation status is of major prognostic and predictive relevance in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma, yet currently depends on invasive tissue sampling. This study investigates deep learning-based strategies for MGMT prediction from multiparametric MRIs, with particular emphasis on robustness and generalizability under heterogeneous, multicenter conditions. A total of 949 glioblastoma cases were analyzed, integrating public benchmark data from the Brain Tumor Segmentation Challenge (BraTS) with multi-institutional private cohorts acquired across diverse scanners and imaging protocols. Four complementary experimental settings were designed to compare reproduced literature baselines, private-only training, whole-brain end-to-end models, and segmentation-guided region-of-interest (ROI) pipelines. Tumor delineation was performed using an nnU-Net framework with expert quality control, and multiple three-dimensional convolutional neural network architectures were evaluated. Model performance was highest on the homogeneous BraTS benchmark, where a whole-brain DenseNet121 achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.80. However, marked performance deterioration was observed when models were evaluated on independent held-out multicenter test set. In contrast, segmentation-guided ROI-based approaches showed a more stable performance profile in this preliminary independent held-out multicenter test. Explicit lesion localization was associated with reduction in false-positive classifications, suggesting a potential benefit for performance stability across heterogeneous datasets, although validation in external cohorts from institutions not represented during training is required. Collectively, these results demonstrate that upstream methodological choices, especially tumor segmentation and ROI definition, remain critical determinants of performance in MRI-based radiogenomic modeling. Future studies should emphasize prospective multicenter validation, domain-shift harmonization, multimodal data integration, and uncertainty-aware deep learning to enhance robustness and interpretability.

candidates.title: A Value-Based Approach to Designing Inclusive Clinical Trials.
candidates.abstract: The underrepresentation of marginalized populations in clinical trials remains a critical issue, limiting the generalizability of findings and exacerbating health disparities. Despite policy efforts to improve diversity, a key challenge remains: how much representation is sufficient? This study addresses this question using a decision-analytic framework that considers both the value of evidence and equity when allocating trial participants across population subgroups. We developed equity-weighted extensions of expected value of sample information (wEVSI) and expected net benefit of sampling (wENBS) to optimize the allocation of trial participants across population subgroups. The framework incorporates subgroup-specific uncertainty, equity weights, common or subgroup-specific treatment decisions, and cross-group information borrowing through Bayesian hierarchical models. wENBS further accounts for the consequences of randomization for trial participants, participation burdens, and trial costs. We illustrated the framework using a stylized 2-subgroup case study that varied the evidence configuration, degree of borrowing, equity weights, recruitment costs, and decision structure. In the main scenario, evidence was more uncertain for the historically marginalized subgroup. Under moderate and near-no borrowing, wENBS was maximized by enrolling this subgroup above its population share. Greater equity weights generally shifted the preferred allocation further toward the marginalized subgroup, whereas higher recruitment costs shifted it modestly toward the other subgroup. Under moderate borrowing, allowing subgroup-specific decisions also supported greater enrollment of the historically marginalized subgroup. Under near-complete borrowing, trial composition had little effect, and no allocation was clearly preferred. Alternative evidence profiles resulted in below-proportional or approximately proportional enrollment or no additional trial when the current evidence was already sufficiently precise. This framework provides a value-based approach to balancing efficiency, equity, and cost in inclusive trial design.
candidates.journal: Medical decision making : an international journal of the Society for Medical Decision Making

candidates.title: Benefits of Intracystic Bleomycin for Symptomatic Recurrent Rathke Cleft Cyst: An Institutional Update.
candidates.abstract: The management of recurrent Rathke cleft cysts (RCC) poses a unique clinical challenge. The mainstay of treatment is reoperation with cyst drainage; however, there is limited evidence evaluating adjuvant pharmaceutical therapy in this patient population. Several studies, including a 2019 study by Ung et al at our institution, suggest a potential benefit of the use of intracystic bleomycin in recurrent RCC. The intracystic application of bleomycin is known to be beneficial in the treatment of cystic craniopharyngioma, however, its role in the treatment of recurrent Rathke cleft cyst remains unclear. To evaluate long-term outcomes of recurrent RCC treated with intracystic bleomycin, building on a 2019 study by our institution which reported no short-term follow-up recurrence. We conducted a retrospective chart review of patients with RCC who underwent surgical resection with intracystic bleomycin between January 2011 and December 2023 by a single surgeon. This study updates our 2019 study which reported no recurrence in 6 patients who received intracystic bleomycin for recurrent RCC. Patient symptom ratings were collected preoperatively and postoperatively. Of 125 patients with a history of surgery for RCC, 29 (23%) experienced radiographic recurrence. Subsequently, 24 of these patients underwent reresection with 20 of these patients receiving intracystic bleomycin at the time of secondary resection. To date, only 2 bleomycin-treated patients experienced recurrence (10%) with a median follow-up of 28.4 [4.0-54.4] months. Compared with historical data which show a 26.2% recurrence rate after secondary resection without adjuvant therapy, our bleomycin-treated cohort demonstrated a lower recurrence rate. The use of intracystic bleomycin seems to be a safe and potentially effective treatment option in patients with recurrent RCC.

candidates.title: Variable Expressivity of von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) Disease Associated with c.499C>T Variant in a Multigenerational Family.
candidates.abstract: von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) disease is an autosomal dominant cancer syndrome caused by germline pathogenic variants in the VHL tumor suppressor gene manifesting as a spectrum of neoplasms, including the central nervous system (CNS) and retinal hemangioblastomas, pheochromocytoma, renal cell carcinoma (RCC), pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (PNETs), and paraganglioma. This study systematically evaluates the clinical, radiological, and molecular genetic profiles of a large multigeneration family harboring the pathogenic variant c.499C>T (p.Arg167Trp). Affected individuals and at-risk family members underwent clinical exome sequencing and targeted cascade molecular testing. Variants were classified according to the 2015 guidelines of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics-Association for Molecular Pathology. Multidisciplinary follow-up encompassed neurological, endocrinological, ophthalmological, and radiological evaluations, including optical coherence tomography and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) surveillance. Among 47 individuals tested across five generations, 23 were confirmed to carry the heterozygous pathogenic variant c.499C>T (p.Arg167Trp) in the VHL gene (NM_000551.4). Among the 23 molecularly confirmed carriers (which included several young carriers still under surveillance), pheochromocytoma was the most prevalent manifestation (5/23), followed by CNS hemangioblastoma (3/23), retinal angioma (2/23), PNET (2/23), and pancreatic cysts (2/23). No RCC was identified among molecularly confirmed carriers. Clinical presentations were consistent with multiple VHL disease subtypes, reflecting broad intrafamilial phenotypic heterogeneity. The c.499C>T (p.Arg167Trp) variant demonstrates remarkable phenotypic variability, ranging from multiple concurrent VHL-associated neoplasms to asymptomatic carrier status within the same family. These findings underscore the necessity of lifelong multidisciplinary surveillance and comprehensive cascade genetic testing in the clinical management of VHL disease.
candidates.journal: Journal of kidney cancer and VHL

candidates.title: Bilateral adrenal diffuse large B-cell lymphoma masquerading as bilateral adrenal metastases: a rare presentation diagnosed by endoscopic ultrasound-guided fine-needle biopsy.
candidates.abstract: Bilateral adrenal diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is an exceedingly rare entity. Presentation as bilateral adrenal masses without an identifiable extra-adrenal primary poses a formidable diagnostic challenge, frequently mimicking adrenal metastases or primary adrenal malignancy. A 70-year-old normotensive, non-diabetic male presented with a one-month history of weight loss, generalized dull abdominal pain, and anorexia. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) revealed bilateral adrenal masses (right 56 × 28 × 55 mm; left 61 × 30 × 54 mm) with imaging characteristics indistinguishable from metastatic disease. Extensive workup-including CT of the neck and chest, colonoscopy, and biochemical adrenal profiling-failed to identify a primary extra-adrenal malignancy or hormonal excess. Endoscopic ultrasound-guided fine-needle biopsy (EUS-FNB) using a 22-gauge needle provided tissue confirming diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) with CD20 and PAX-5 positivity. The patient was referred to oncology and commenced on rituximab-based chemotherapy. This case underscores the indispensable role of EUS-guided tissue sampling in the evaluation of bilateral adrenal masses when non-invasive workup is inconclusive. Early tissue diagnosis of adrenal DLBCL is critical, as it is a potentially curable disease amenable to immunochemotherapy rather than surgery.

candidates.title: Recovery of adrenal function following sequential spontaneous bilateral adrenal hemorrhage.
candidates.abstract: Adrenal hemorrhage is uncommon; bilateral involvement is even rarer and can result in adrenal crisis. A 55-year-old man presented with severe atraumatic flank and low back pain; computed tomography of the abdomen revealed acute left adrenal hemorrhage. He was managed conservatively. Seven days after initial presentation, he returned with contralateral flank pain; repeat imaging demonstrated a new right adrenal hemorrhage with persistent left hemorrhage. He developed nausea, vomiting, headache, and hyponatremia; the morning cortisol was 8.99 µg/dL (248 nmol/L; reference range, 5-25 µg/dL [138-690 nmol/L]). He was admitted to the intensive care unit and treated with stress-dose hydrocortisone. Fludrocortisone was initiated as plasma renin activity was elevated. Extensive evaluation for an underlying etiology for adrenal hemorrhage was unrevealing. Serial imaging showed near-complete resolution of hematomas. Follow-up testing approximately a year after initial presentation demonstrated complete recovery of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis, allowing for discontinuation of hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone. This case highlights the need for repeat imaging and close biochemical monitoring for adrenal insufficiency and HPA axis recovery following bilateral adrenal hemorrhage.

candidates.title: Laser Force Cytology for In-Process Monitoring of High-Titer Orf Virus Vectors: Process Integration with Optimized Nuclease Treatment and Clarification in Pharmaceutical Manufacturing.
candidates.abstract: Orf virus (ORFV) is a versatile viral vector platform with applications in vaccine development and oncolytic therapy. Its large poxviral genome allows for the insertion and expression of multiple heterologous transgenes, making ORFV particularly attractive for the development of recombinant vaccines and therapeutic vectors. Efficient manufacturing of ORFV-based products requires high infectious virus yields while maintaining robust downstream processing and product recovery. In this study, we used a high-titer ORFV harvest to investigate nuclease treatment and clarification as key early downstream processing steps. Host cells were monitored during the infection phase using Laser Force Cytology to support the identification of an optimal harvest time. In addition, crude harvest pretreatment was optimized using enhanced NaCl concentrations and endonuclease treatment before clarification filtration. Amplification of ORFV viral vectors in HEK293F derivatives resulted in peak infectious titers of up to 3.3 × 109 IU mL-1. The addition of NaCl allowed for efficient degradation of DNA impurities by Denarase® High Salt while stabilizing the ORFV vector. Optimal enzyme performance was observed using 550 mM NaCl and 90 U mL-1 Denarase® High Salt for 7 h at 21 °C, resulting in 92% depletion of residual double-stranded DNA (dsDNA). For clarification filtration, a combination of polypropylene-based depth filters with retention rates of 5 and 0.5 µm recovered 91% of ORFV while depleting 33% dsDNA and 36% protein. This comprehensive data define optimized harvest timing, nuclease treatment and the clarification strategy of high-titer ORFV material, paving the way for pharmaceutical manufacturing of ORFV vectors.

candidates.title: A Pooled Analysis of Streptococcus pneumoniae Serotype Distribution Reveals an Increasing Proportion of Non-Vaccine Serotypes Among Chinese Children with Invasive Pneumococcal Disease, 2009-2024.
candidates.abstract: Objective: To describe the distribution of non-vaccine serotypes (NVTs) causing pediatric IPD in China, we conducted a retrospective multi-center pooled analysis of non-PCV13 Streptococcus pneumoniae isolates from 2009 to 2024. Methods: We pooled individual-level data from 863 pediatric IPD cases across the Chinese mainland (2009-2024). After deduplication and laboratory re-verification, 103 unique non-PCV13 isolates from 15 cities were included for serotyping, genotyping, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing. Data from the late-PCV13 period (2020-2024) were compared with pre- (2009-2016) and early-PCV13 periods (2017-2019). Results: Among 863 IPD strains, 121 (14.0%) were non-PCV13; 103 unique isolates were analyzed. The proportion of non-PCV13 isolates increased from 7.5% (2009-2016) to 11.0% (2017-2019) and 17.8% (2020-2024) (p < 0.01) among characterised isolates. These isolates comprised 36 serotypes, dominated by 15A (13.6%), 15B (8.7%), 15C (7.8%), and 23A (7.8%). PCV20-extended serotypes accounted for only 19.4%. Twenty-two serotypes emerged post-PCV13 introduction. Sixty-six sequence types (STs) were identified, led by ST11972 (8.7%), ST8589 (7.8%), and ST9396 (4.9%). Erythromycin and clindamycin resistance rates were 94.2% and 90.3%, respectively. Conclusions: Among available pediatric IPD isolates in mainland China, the relative proportion of non-PCV13 serotypes increased over time, although this trend cannot currently be accurately quantified or confirmed as being related to changes in population-level IPD incidence or to vaccine-driven serotype replacement. The considerable serotype and genotype diversity poses substantial challenges for expanded vaccine formulations and future surveillance.

candidates.title: Case report: Glycemic instability despite fasting C-peptide recovery during sequential somatostatin receptor ligand therapy in acromegaly with diabetes.
candidates.abstract: Somatostatin receptor ligands (SRLs) may improve glucose metabolism by reducing growth hormone excess, but they can also suppress insulin secretion. Severe hyperglycemia is well recognized with pasireotide. Less is known about glycemic stability after recovery from severe decompensation and during later changes in SRL therapy. A 32-year-old woman with diabetes had persistent acromegaly despite transsphenoidal surgery, Gamma Knife radiosurgery, cabergoline, octreotide, and lanreotide. Pasireotide long-acting release 40 mg lowered growth hormone and insulin-like growth factor 1, but approximately 1 month later was followed by diabetic ketoacidosis and a fasting C-peptide of 0.38 ng/mL. Pasireotide was stopped, insulin-based treatment was given, and octreotide was resumed. Fasting C-peptide increased to 3.09 ng/mL within 2 months. During lanreotide re-exposure in 2025, HbA1c was 9.3% despite fasting C-peptide within the reference interval and no parallel deterioration in biochemical disease control. After lanreotide withdrawal and adjustment of diabetes therapy, intermittent hyperglycemia continued, although HbA1c decreased to 6.3% by July 2026. Return of fasting C-peptide into the reference interval after pasireotide-associated diabetic ketoacidosis did not predict sustained glycemic stability in this patient. The later deterioration during lanreotide therapy was temporally associated with treatment but does not establish causality. The overall course is more consistent with persistent metabolic vulnerability despite normalization of fasting C-peptide than with confirmed recurrent SRL-induced dysglycemia. Glucose monitoring should be intensified when an SRL is started or changed in patients with diabetes or previous ketosis.

candidates.title: Diagnostic and Translational Challenges in Canine Endocrine and Neuroendocrine Neoplasms: A Comparative Pathology Perspective.
candidates.abstract: The recognition and detection of endocrine and neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs) in dogs and humans is challenging. This is, in part, because some are non-functional, and where hormone hypersecretion occurs, it can lead to a great variety of clinical syndromes. Additionally, metastatic patterns vary according to the primary anatomical site, and the typically slow growth of many endocrine tumours/NENs may lead to underestimation of biological aggressiveness and misclassification as benign disease. In human medicine, diagnostic evaluation relies on a comprehensive, anatomical site-specific histopathologic framework, incorporating immunohistochemistry as formalised in the 2025 World Health Organisation classification of endocrine tumours/NENs. In contrast, veterinary diagnostic frameworks for canine endocrine tumours/NENs remain comparatively underdeveloped, with limited standardisation of terminology, grading systems, and validated cut-off values. This review aims to raise awareness of key diagnostic challenges associated with the most clinically prevalent canine endocrine tumours/NENs: insulinoma, phaeochromocytoma and cortisol-producing adrenocortical tumours. Emphasis is placed on histopathological characterisation using immunohistochemistry, drawing parallels with established human diagnostic algorithms where appropriate. By synthesising current knowledge from human and canine pathology, this review highlights critical gaps in veterinary diagnostic practice and identifies opportunities for harmonisation of classification strategies. The development of standardised diagnostic guidelines has the potential not only to improve clinical management of affected dogs but also to strengthen the translational value of spontaneous canine endocrine tumours/NENs within the field of comparative oncology and One Medicine.

candidates.title: Herpes Zoster Vaccination and Dementia Risk: A Systematic Review of Natural Experiments and Cohort Evidence.
candidates.abstract: Background/Objectives: More than 55 million people live with dementia, and no treatment halts its progression, which makes prevention the priority. Herpes zoster (HZ) results from reactivation of varicella-zoster virus (VZV) and has been linked to a higher dementia risk. Vaccination is already recommended for HZ and postherpetic neuralgia; whether it also protects cognition remains unclear. We critically appraise the evidence linking HZ vaccination to dementia risk across study designs. Methods: Following the PRISMA 2020 statement, we searched PubMed/MEDLINE and Europe PMC from 1 January 2015 to 29 October 2026 with forward citation searching and identified 36 eligible reports: 25 primary investigations (four natural experiments using date-of-birth eligibility cutoffs, one quasi-experimental analysis of a vaccine transition, 17 cohort studies, two nested case-control analyses, one cross-sectional survey; 20 with vaccination as the exposure; and five with infection as the exposure) and 11 secondary syntheses (10 systematic reviews or meta-analyses and one secondary quantification). Six narrative reviews served only as contextual references and were not counted. Results: Natural experiments report a consistent reduction in incident dementia, 8.5% (95% CI 1.9-15.1) on an eligibility basis and about 20% when scaled to vaccine receipt. Cohort analyses show larger, more variable reductions (24% to 51%), part of which reflects healthy vaccinee bias; the association persists, attenuated, against negative-control vaccines. Candidate mechanisms include VZV-specific immunity and broader immune modulation. Conclusions: The association between HZ vaccination and lower subsequent dementia risk is consistent in direction, biologically plausible, and modest in size, but every dementia outcome was graded very low certainty, so causality and magnitude both remain uncertain, and the evidence does not support a dementia-prevention indication. Randomized trials, mechanistic studies, and designs separating an effect on onset from an effect on the timing of diagnosis are needed. Retrospective registration: OSF Registries (10.17605/OSF.IO/MBXWE).

candidates.title: Prognostic Significance of Tertiary Lymphoid Structures in Invasive Breast Cancer.
candidates.abstract: Tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) are organized immune aggregates associated with improved outcomes in several solid tumors. Their significance in invasive breast cancer remains poorly characterized. TLS were evaluated in 1,703 breast tumors from the Carolina Breast Cancer Study (CBCS) using H&E whole-slide image annotation (training set, n=842) and bulk RNA profiling to develop an RNA-based TLS classifier tested in a holdout set (n=861). Associations with clinicopathologic features and progression-free survival (PFS) were assessed using multinomial logistic and Cox models. In the I-SPY2 neoadjuvant trial cohort (N=985), associations with pathologic complete response (pCR) were assessed by logistic regression, adjusted for treatment arm. TLS were associated with younger age, Black race, high tumor grade, hormone receptor (HR)-negativity, and stromal tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs). In HR-negative disease, histologic mTLS presence was associated with improved PFS (HR=0.41, 95% CI: 0.17-0.96). RNA-based mTLS classification (n=1,703) was associated with improved PFS overall and in HER2-positive and triple negative disease (HRs 0.32-0.51). In I-SPY2, RNA-based mTLS class was associated with increased odds of pCR in HR-negative (OR=1.59, 95% CI: 1.05-2.41) and HER2-positive (OR=2.02, 95% CI: 1.14-3.62) tumors; after adjustment for treatment arm, this association remained significant in HER2-positive disease (OR=2.07, 95% CI: 1.14-3.80). mTLS demonstrate prognostic value in HR-negative breast cancer and association with neoadjuvant treatment response in HER2-positive disease. These findings support mature TLS as prognostically informative in breast cancer and suggest that transcriptomic TLS classification warrants prospective evaluation as a predictive biomarker in HER2-positive disease.

candidates.title: Papillary craniopharyngioma mistaken for recurrent Rathke's cleft cyst: a case report of a seven-year diagnostic pitfall involving BRAF V600E testing.
candidates.abstract: Rathke's cleft cysts (RCC) and craniopharyngiomas are clinically, radiologically and histopathologically similar lesions that are difficult to distinguish and require different surgical treatments. Many authors support the hypothesis that these represent two spectra of the same pathology. We present the case of a 53-year-old man who, because of general malaise, was examined by an endocrinologist and found to have partial hypopituitarism and indirect hyperprolactinemia. Consequently, he underwent a head MRI, which revealed an intra-suprasellar cystic lesion. Surgical fenestration of the cyst was performed, and tissue samples were collected for histopathological examination, which confirmed a diagnosis of RCC. Over the years, follow-up imaging revealed a recurrent, enlarging cyst; therefore, the patient underwent reoperation 7.5 years later. This time, histology revealed a papillary craniopharyngioma (PC). Re-examination of the specimen from the first surgery also confirmed presence of PC on the same specimen section as RCC, with the initial false-negative result attributed to suboptimal staining. Apparent progression from RCC to craniopharyngioma should prompt re-examination of the original pathology before it is interpreted as true transformation. In our patient, conservative fenestration was followed by recovery of corticotroph function that lasted seven years, whereas subsequent radical surgery resulted in new corticotroph and thyrotroph deficiency without complete resection, highlighting the need for caution with early aggressive surgery in cystic sellar lesions of uncertain histology.

candidates.title: Clinical characteristics and management of nivolumab-induced hypophysitis: retrospective analysis based on case reports.
candidates.abstract: Nivolumab-associated hypophysitis is a rare endocrine immune-related adverse event with incompletely defined clinical characteristics and management. This study aimed to synthesize patient-level evidence to clarify its presentation, treatment, and clinical outcomes, thereby facilitating earlier recognition and evidence-based management. We conducted a retrospective, case-based synthesis of nivolumab-induced hypophysitis. PubMed, EMBASE, Web of Science, WanFang Data, and CNKI were systematically searched for reports published up to Jan 31, 2026, using a combination of MeSH terms: ("nivolumab" OR "PD-1 inhibitor" OR "programmed death-1 inhibitor" OR "immune checkpoint inhibitor" OR "ICI") AND ("hypophysitis" OR "pituitary inflammation" OR "hypopituitarism") AND ("immune-related adverse event" OR "irAE" OR "endocrinopathy"). Among 2,264 records screened, 38 case reports and case series comprising 40 patients were included in the final analysis. Median age was 62 years (range 26-84), and 72.5% were male. Hypophysitis occurred most often in melanoma (42.5%) and renal cell carcinoma (30.0%), with a median onset of 20 weeks. Fatigue (82.5%), anorexia/nausea (65.0%), and hyponatremia (42.5%) were common; pituitary MRI abnormalities were reported in 46.2%. Endocrine testing mainly showed central adrenal insufficiency with central hypothyroidism; median cortisol and ACTH were 2.9 µg/dL and 38.0 pg/mL. All patients received corticosteroids, 35.0% received levothyroxine, and nivolumab was discontinued in 80.0%. Among 16 rechallenged patients, relapse occurred in 18.8%. Clinical improvement was frequent (92.5%), whereas full hormonal recovery was uncommon. Nivolumab-induced hypophysitis primarily involves the corticotropic axis. Early hormonal evaluation and imaging are essential. Corticosteroids remain the mainstay of treatment, and long-term hormone replacement is often necessary. Rechallenge with nivolumab may be considered in selected patients, but requires careful risk-benefit assessment. Not applicable.

candidates.title: Reconstruction with a novel pedicled mucoperiosteal hinge flap and dura suturing: a new minimally invasive concept and closure technique for endoscopic endonasal surgery.
candidates.abstract: The authors aimed to evaluate their experience with the minimally invasive reconstruction technique using pedicled mucoperiostea hinge flap (PMHF) with dura suturing after EES. Outcomes were compared with those of the traditional reconstruction using the NSF. The authors conducted a retrospective cohort study involving 33 consecutive patients who underwent EES for pituitary adenoma resection. All these 33 patients were reconstructed with pedicled mucoperiosteal hinge flap with dura suturing and were compared with 32 consecutive patients treated previously using NSF technique. Surgical videos and electronic medical records were reviewed to assess operative times and postoperative outcomes, which were compared between the groups, with a particular focus on nasal function, assessed using the Endoscopic Endonasal Sinus and Skull Base Surgery Questionnaire (EES-Q). Demographics of the two groups were broadly similar. Among the 33 patients using PMHF with dura suturing, the average operative time decreased with experience, showing a trend of improved efficiency. No significant difference was observed between two groups in terms of total operative time. One postoperative CSF leak (3%) was observed in PMHF group, while 2 postoperative CSF leak (6%) occurred in group using NSF (P = 0.61). Importantly, patients who underwent reconstruction with pedicled mucoperiosteal hinge flap with dura suturing reported significantly lower EES-Q scores overall (p < 0.01), with better outcomes in all domains (p < 0.01). This technique provides a reliable method for preventing postoperative CSF leak and a less invasive option, ultimately contributing to the preservation of the patient's quality of life (QOL).

candidates.title: Vertebral fractures unmasking Cushing disease: an unexpected argument for secondary osteoporosis screening.
candidates.abstract: Osteoporosis poses a substantial health and financial burden. Although secondary causes are more common in men, they are screened less for osteoporosis than their female counterparts. We present the case of a 70-year-old man with a history of an adrenal incidentaloma with a recent diagnosis of 2 vertebral fractures. Initial workup revealed adrenocorticotropic hormone-dependent hypercortisolism. Imaging confirmed a pituitary macroadenoma, suggestive of Cushing disease (CD). Lifestyle modifications, calcium and vitamin D supplementation, and intravenous zoledronic acid were initiated to treat the severe osteoporosis. Pituitary surgery was carried out, with pathology revealing a Crooke cell adenoma. This case illustrates the importance of screening for osteoporosis in men, including thorough evaluation to rule out secondary causes. Moreover, a critical evaluation of the current approach to bone health in CD is provided.

candidates.title: Kidney biopsy unveiled: multifactorial damage in immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy, a case report.
candidates.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have revolutionized cancer treatment by enhancing anti-tumor immunity, but may cause immune-related adverse events (IRAEs) in up to 40% of patients. Renal involvement occurs in 1-5% of cases and includes a spectrum of immune-mediated injuries, most commonly acute interstitial nephritis (AIN). We report the case of a 79-year-old man with stage G3A chronic kidney disease and biphasic pleural mesothelioma treated with dual ICI therapy. Eleven days after treatment initiation, he developed acute kidney injury (AKI) and severe hypercalcemia with neurological symptoms. A comprehensive diagnostic work-up excluded the most common causes of hypercalcemia, raising suspicion of an immune-mediated mechanism. Because renal dysfunction persisted despite supportive measures, a kidney biopsy was performed and showed granulomatous AIN with tubular calcium deposition and non-necrotizing epithelioid granulomas, findings consistent, although uncommon, with ICI-related nephrotoxicity. Further imaging findings strongly supported central adrenal insufficiency secondary to hypophysitis as the underlying cause of hypercalcemia. Corticosteroid therapy led to marked clinical improvement, with complete recovery of renal function and resolution of hypercalcemia. This case highlights the diagnostic and prognostic value of kidney biopsy in ICI-associated AKI, as histological findings clarified the interplay between immune-mediated nephrotoxicity, hypercalcemia, and pre-existing CKD, thereby guiding tailored nephrological and oncological management. It also emphasizes that, in patients receiving ICIs, hypercalcemia should raise suspicion for central adrenal insufficiency due to hypophysitis.

candidates.title: Giant adrenal teratoma mimicking renal angiomyolipoma during pregnancy with coexisting fetal pulmonary sequestration: a case report.
candidates.abstract: Adrenal tumors during pregnancy are rare, but their detection is increasing due to prenatal imaging. Retroperitoneal fat-containing tumors, such as mature teratomas, can easily mimic renal angiomyolipoma (RAML), especially when the gravid uterus displaces anatomical landmarks. Excluding functional tumors (e.g., pheochromocytoma) is critical to prevent lethal hypertensive crises and guide multidisciplinary team (MDT) management. A 31-year-old primigravida (12 weeks' gestation) presented with a 9.8 × 13.3 × 10.9 cm fat-containing right retroperitoneal mass on MRI, mimicking renal angiomyolipoma or teratoma. Concurrently, fetal ultrasound at 22 + 4 weeks identified an incidental left-sided fetal pulmonary sequestration. Normal catecholamine and cortisol levels confirmed a non-functional tumor, warranting a multidisciplinary team (MDT) strategy of watchful waiting. The patient successfully delivered a live infant via elective cesarean section at 37 + 1 weeks. Postpartum, she underwent elective laparoscopic resection of the retroperitoneal tumor. Intraoperatively, the massive tumor encased the inferior vena cava (IVC) and right renal vein with dense adhesions. A laceration occurred on the posterior wall of the IVC during dissection, which was successfully repaired using vascular sutures without significant blood loss (200 mL). Postoperative pathology confirmed a mature adrenal teratoma. Both mother and neonate showed excellent outcomes during follow-up. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of differentiating giant fat-containing retroperitoneal tumors during pregnancy. For non-functional retroperitoneal tumors without signs of malignancy, delaying surgery until the postpartum period is a safe strategy. In cases involving major vascular encasement, the surgical team must be fully prepared to manage unexpected vascular injuries. A multidisciplinary approach is highly recommended to optimize outcomes for rare maternal tumors and incidental fetal anomalies.

candidates.title: A Sequential Benznidazole-Vaccine-Benznidazole Regimen Enhances Therapeutic Efficacy Against Chronic Trypanosoma cruzi Infection in Mice.
candidates.abstract: Background/Objectives: Chronic Chagas cardiomyopathy (CCC), caused by Trypanosoma cruzi (T. cruzi), remains a major public health challenge and a leading cause of heart failure, with this chronic stage representing the period when most patients are diagnosed and require clinical intervention. However, the efficacy of the available parasiticidal drugs, benznidazole (BZL) and nifurtimox during chronic infection is limited and new therapeutic approaches are needed. In this study, we evaluated a novel sequential chemo-immunotherapeutic strategy (BZL → Vac → BZL) designed to shorten benznidazole treatment duration to minimize drug-related adverse effects by leveraging the synergistic potential of both treatments. Methods: BALB/c mice chronically infected with T. cruzi were used as model. A long-term sequential regimen was evaluated and compared 190 days post-infection with uninfected, untreated infected (Tc), monotherapy (BZL or TSNt-ISPA vaccine), and combined (Vac → BZL) controls. The sequential treatment consisted of an initial short cycle of oral BZL, three subcutaneous immunizations with the TSNt-ISPA vaccine, and a final BZL booster. Cardiac parasite load and cytokine expression (qPCR), inflammation and fibrosis (histopathology), electrocardiograms (ECG), specific antibodies (ELISA), and splenic cellular response (flow cytometry) were analyzed. Results: The BZL-Vac → BZL scheme significantly reduced cardiac parasite load, achieving undetectability in some animals. Combined therapies (Vac → BZL and BZL → Vac → BZL) significantly attenuated myocardial inflammation and fibrosis, improving P-wave duration and the QTc interval. The sequential treatment induced a robust Th1-associated humoral response (IgG2a) and a balanced cellular profile, uniquely increasing splenic IL-10-producing CD4+ T cells, TNF-α-producing CD8+ T cells, and cardiac IL-10 and Foxp3 expression. Conclusions: The temporal integration of fractionated benznidazole and TSNt-ISPA immunotherapy protects myocardial integrity and function through an effector immune response under strict regulatory control.

candidates.title: Pituitary Stalk Interruption Syndrome Presenting as Primary Amenorrhea: Magnetic Resonance Imaging Demonstration of the Characteristic Diagnostic Triad.
candidates.abstract: Pituitary stalk interruption syndrome (PSIS) is a rare congenital pituitary malformation characterized by the triad of anterior pituitary hypoplasia, an absent or interrupted pituitary stalk, and an ectopic posterior pituitary. We report the case of a 21-year-old woman who presented with primary amenorrhea and poorly developed secondary sexual characteristics. Hormonal evaluation revealed central hypothyroidism, markedly reduced morning serum cortisol, and suppressed gonadotropin levels, indicating hypopituitarism with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism. Pelvic ultrasonography demonstrated a markedly hypoplastic uterus and bilaterally small ovaries. Magnetic resonance imaging of the sellar region revealed a hypoplastic anterior pituitary gland, nonvisualization of the pituitary stalk, and an ectopic posterior pituitary bright spot at the median eminence beneath the optic chiasm. These characteristic imaging findings established the diagnosis of PSIS. This case highlights the importance of considering PSIS in women presenting with primary amenorrhea and delayed pubertal development. Recognition of the characteristic magnetic resonance imaging triad facilitates timely endocrine evaluation, hormone replacement therapy, and long-term follow-up. RésuméLe syndrome d’interruption de la tige pituitaire (SITP) est une malformation congénitale rare de l’hypophyse, caractérisée par une triade associant une hypoplasie de l’antéhypophyse, une absence ou une interruption de la tige pituitaire et une neurohypophyse ectopique. Nous rapportons le cas d’une femme de 21 ans consultant pour une aménorrhée primaire et un développement insuffisant des caractères sexuels secondaires. Le bilan hormonal a révélé une hypothyroïdie centrale, une diminution marquée du cortisol sérique matinal et une suppression des taux de gonadotrophines, en faveur d’un hypopituitarisme associé à un hypogonadisme hypogonadotrope. L’échographie pelvienne a montré un utérus très hypoplasique et des ovaires bilatéralement de petite taille. L’imagerie par résonance magnétique (IRM) de la région sellaire a mis en évidence une hypoplasie de l’antéhypophyse, une absence de visualisation de la tige pituitaire et un hypersignal spontané T1 ectopique de la neurohypophyse au niveau de l’éminence médiane, sous le chiasma optique. Ces signes radiologiques caractéristiques ont permis d’établir le diagnostic de SITP. Ce cas souligne l’importance d’évoquer le SITP chez les femmes présentant une aménorrhée primaire et un retard du développement pubertaire. La reconnaissance de la triade caractéristique à l’IRM permet une évaluation endocrinienne précoce, l’instauration d’un traitement hormonal substitutif et un suivi à long terme.

candidates.title: Radiosurgery facilitates pharmacotherapy withdrawal in acromegaly: long-term outcomes.
candidates.abstract: Early and sustained biochemical control is the therapeutic goal in acromegaly. While transsphenoidal surgery is the first-line treatment, many patients require multimodal therapy. The role of stereotactic radiosurgery in facilitating pharmacotherapy withdrawal has not been well characterised. In this retrospective single-centre cohort study, we evaluated 136 patients with acromegaly who underwent transsphenoidal surgery between 2002 and 2021 and were followed through January 2026. Outcomes included IGF-1 normalization, withdrawal of medical therapy after Leksell Gamma Knife radiosurgery (LGK), pituitary function, and treatment-related complications. Postoperative IGF-1 normalization was achieved in 60/136 patients (44.1%). Overall, 66/136 patients (48.5%) underwent LGK. Among patients treated with LGK and concomitant pharmacotherapy, the median time to IGF-1 normalization was 8 months, and 50/62 (80.6%) discontinued medical therapy, with a median time to withdrawal of 50.5 months (IQR 17-79.5). Dopamine agonist monotherapy was sufficient in 27/71 patients (38.0%) requiring postoperative pharmacotherapy. Clinically relevant hypopituitarism developed in 8/66 patients (12.1%) after LGK. At final follow-up, IGF-1 normalization was achieved in 133/136 patients (97.8%), and 116/136 (85.3%) remained controlled without ongoing IGF-1-lowering therapy. Multimodal treatment provides durable long-term control of acromegaly. In patients with persistent disease after surgery, LGK contributes to sustained biochemical disease control and facilitates progressive pharmacotherapy de-escalation, with treatment withdrawal achieved in a substantial proportion of patients. Dopamine agonists represent an effective oral option for selected patients with mild residual disease activity.

candidates.title: Metabolic Continuity in Cancer Vaccination.
candidates.abstract: Cancer vaccines can generate durable, tumor-specific T-cell responses, yet immunogenicity remains an imperfect surrogate for tumor control. An important, incompletely characterized contributor may be the metabolic fitness of the vaccine-induced immune response. Dendritic-cell activation, T-cell clonal expansion, effector differentiation, trafficking, tissue residency, tumor entry, cytotoxicity, and memory formation each impose distinct bioenergetic and biosynthetic requirements. These requirements are progressively challenged in tumors by nutrient competition, hypoxia, lactate and acidosis, adenosine, lipid stress, amino-acid depletion, mitochondrial dysfunction, and metabolically adapted suppressive cells. Here, we use metabolic continuity as a design principle for cancer vaccination: successful therapy requires preservation of metabolic competence from antigen presentation through intratumoral tumor killing and durable memory. We further use the term shared nutrient-dependency paradox to highlight a translational problem: pathways considered attractive tumor targets, including amino-acid transport and mTOR-linked nutrient sensing, may also be required by newly activated antitumor T cells. LAT1/SLC7A5 provides a particularly instructive example because it supports large neutral amino-acid uptake in both malignant cells and activated cytotoxic lymphocytes. We argue that metabolic interventions should therefore be judged by a vaccine-specific metabolic therapeutic index, not by tumor-cell growth inhibition alone. The most rational combinations will exploit differences in metabolic plasticity, cellular selectivity, anatomical compartment, and treatment timing. Incorporating metabolic biomarkers into vaccine trials could shift cancer vaccination from an antigen-centric intervention toward a metabolically engineered immune response.

candidates.title: Patients with acromegaly who underwent surgery at Haukeland University Hospital, 2015-2024.
candidates.abstract: Acromegaly is a rare disease. The aim of this study was to describe the clinical characteristics, course of treatment and outcomes of patients who underwent surgery for acromegaly at Haukeland University Hospital in the period 2015-2024. A retrospective review of medical records of patients who underwent surgery for acromegaly between 1. January 2015 and 31 December 2024. A total of 23 patients were included in the study, 11 of whom were women (48 %). The median age at diagnosis was 60 years (range 26-81). Macroadenomas were identified in 17 patients (74 %). Six patients (26 %) were in remission at the 3-month follow-up after primary surgery. At the last follow-up, after a median of 70 months (range 7-126), nine patients (39 %) were in remission. Fourteen patients received further treatment in the form of pharmacotherapy, repeat surgery and/or radiotherapy. Acromegaly is a rare disease, and the high proportion of macroadenomas suggests late diagnosis. Many patients do not achieve remission after surgery and require further treatment to control the disease.
